stories.title: Crew from Nasa's simulated Mars mission emerges after 378 days in isolation
summary: This was Nasa’s second ​Chapea mission, with another four-person ⁠crew in isolation at Johnson Space Centre for 378 days spanning 2023 and 2024.
Vanessa Wyche, director of the Johnson Space Centre, greeted the crew members when they exited isolation.
Wyche said the lessons learned from ⁠the Chapea crew and their experiences will help pave the way for the missions first ​to the moon and “one day, Mars”.

stories.title: Pakistan responds to unprovoked firing from Afghan posts along border in Lower South Waziristan: DC
summary: Pakistani security forces have responded to unprovoked firing from the Afghan border posts, the deputy commissioner of Lower South Waziristan district said on Sunday.

We’re against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets.” Pak-Afghan tensions Ties between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism.
On Oct 17, state media reported that Pakistani security forces responded to unprovoked fire from the Afghan side along the border in Kurram.

stories.title: Polio case from KP's Khyber takes nationwide tally for 2026 to eight
summary: The latest case was from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Khyber district, where the affected child is a 13-month-old girl from Union Council Janbaz-B in the Bara tehsil, according to the Pakistan Polio Eradication Programme (PPEP).

The Pakistan Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI) has launched a case investigation and is analysing the best science-based response to tackle and prevent further transmission, including targeted vaccination activities and support to strengthen routine immunisation.

In 2026 so far, Pakistan has already implemented four large-scale polio campaigns, protecting more than 45 million children multiple times, alongside smaller targeted campaigns to administer oral and injectable vaccines in high-risk areas, including the Peshawar Block.

stories.title: ‘We’re technology-savvy’: DG ISPR says Pakistan ahead of India, Afghan Taliban in operational readiness
summary: Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has affirmed that Pakistan is “much ahead” in operational readiness compared to the Afghan Taliban and India, adding that the country’s military is adopting emerging technologies.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan.

Responding to a question about whether isolating the Afghan Taliban could further harm the neighbouring country, particularly its farmers affected by cuts in foreign aid, Lt Gen Chaudhry voiced Pakistan’s opposition to isolating Afghanistan. “I fully agree.

stories.title: Pakistan's embassy in Tehran refutes rumours of people 'attacking' its ambassador to Iran
summary: Pakistan’s embassy in Iran on Sunday refuted rumours of an attack on Ambassador Imran Ahmed Siddiqui in Tehran, terming them “baseless”.
In a post on X, the embassy said it had taken note of “certain reports circulating in social media and other forums” concerning the Pakistani ambassador to Iran.

The account claimed that Siddiqui was taken to a nearby hospital for medical treatment. “The embassy categorically clarifies that these reports are baseless and factually incorrect,” the post by Pakistan’s embassy in Tehran said.

stories.title: Sialkot police say 6 held as TikToker nominated in case over stampede at mehndi event
summary: NAROWAL: Sialkot police on Sunday said they had arrested six suspects and registered a case after a stampede at a TikToker’s mehndi (henna) event, the deaths from which have risen to two.
TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, known as “Mr Pattlo”, had announced holding a mehndi event and prize-distribution ceremony at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road on Friday night.

NOC revoked According to a spokesperson for the Sialkot district administration, a no-objection certificate (NOC) had been issued to the TikToker for holding a mehfil-i-samaa (a gathering for devotional music/poetry) during a private event within an enclosed space in Daska.

stories.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
summary: Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets.
In the most intense phase of the war, which began on Feb 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region.
Since the war began, Iran has claimed control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit, and repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to cross without its authorisation.

stories.title: Terrorist attacks drop by 37pc in October: PICSS
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators during October, with terrorist attacks declining by 37 per cent compared with September, it emerged on Sunday.

According to PICSS, terrorist attacks and security forces’ counterterrorism operations collectively resulted in deaths of 53 security forces personnel, 45 civilians and five peace committee members, while 169 terrorists were killed.
The combined number of injuries from terrorist attacks and security operations also reached a 12-month low, as did injuries among security forces personnel. — Screengrab via PICSS report.

stories.title: Pakistan’s past and future make a bid for the present
summary: Pakistan does not have a lot of time left with Fakhar.
But if yesterday showed anything, apart from reaffirming what Fakhar means to a Pakistan side, it was that Pakistan don’t have to be starved of time.
Saad was Pakistan’s U-19 captain, and made his debut earlier in this tri-series.

stories.title: US hears Pakistan’s concerns over terrorism from Afghanistan, would play ‘productive role’ if there is one: Rubio
summary: Mentioning that the US did not “necessarily [have] the closest relationship” with the Afghan Taliban, Rubio added: “We’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to.

For their part, the Afghan Taliban have avoided taking a categorical position on the TTP and other groups, while rejecting Islamabad’s allegations that Afghanistan is being used as a base for attacks against Pakistan.

On Saturday, Pakistan’s information ministry rebuked the Afghan Taliban’s stance on the ongoing conflict between the two countries, assailing its “persistent refusal to address terrorism” emanating from Afghanistan’s soil.

stories.title: Upper Dir police claim arresting 5 suspects over alleged assault of minor boy
summary: LOWER DIR: Police in Upper Dir said on Sunday they have arrested five of the six suspects over the alleged assault and intimidation of a teenage boy, a purported video of which was circulated on social media.
The incident took place on Oct 25, according to a first information report (FIR), dated Oct 30 and seen by Dawn, filed by Wari police on the boy’s complaint.

In the FIR, the boy alleged that on the day of the incident, a friend of his called him to a place where two men, including an unidentified tehsildar, forcibly made him board a car and took him to an under-construction house in Shinkarai.

stories.title: Qatar offers 30-day tourist visa on arrival to Pakistani travellers subject to conditions
summary: Pakistani nationals travelling to Qatar can obtain a 30-day tourist visa on arrival, provided they meet a set of requirements, Doha News reported on Sunday, citing the country's Ministry of Interior (MoI).
According to the ministry's website, applicants must have at least 5,000 Qatari riyals in cash or an equivalent amount available through a valid credit card to qualify for the visa.
The visa is valid for 30 days and can be extended for a further 30 days, provided travellers have a confirmed return ticket before the extension is granted, according to the ministry.

stories.title: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts: DC South Waziristan
summary: Security forces responded to unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts near Angoor Adda in South Waziristan, forcing Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon their positions, Lower South Waziristan deputy commissioner said on Sunday.
Also Read: Pakistan slams Afghan Taliban’s 'latest fabrication of lies' on Angoor Adda clashes The latest development comes amid heightened tensions along the border in recent days.

Earlier in September this year, Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists following a series of deadly attacks in K-P.

stories.title: PIA's first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner arrives in Islamabad
summary: Pakistan International Airlines’ (PIA) first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, acquired on lease last month, arrived in Islamabad from London as flight PK786 on Sunday.
A PIA spokesperson, in a statement, said that the carrier is the first Pakistani airline to have added a Boeing 787-9 to its fleet.
A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the airline’s expansion.

stories.title: Pakistan becomes chair of G-24 bloc of developing nations, reaffirms pledge to fairer global financial system
summary: Aurangzeb outlined three strategic priorities for Pakistan under the G-24 chairmanship: placing development at the centre of global economic policymaking, strengthening multilateral frameworks, and advancing a development-oriented international financial architecture.

The finance minister emphasised aligning financial stability with long-term development objectives, drawing on Pakistan’s experience with economic stabilisation, reform and resilience, the statement said.

The premier further commended the team for ensuring “impactful” participation at the recently held annual meetings of the World Bank and the IMF, which he said helped Pakistan secure a “prominent position in the economic leadership of developing nations”.

stories.title: Cyber safety
summary: WHILE the state’s proposal to create a Cybersecurity and Social Media Awareness Council envisages needed interventions to protect children from online harm, the same body’s focus on ‘fake news’ — as described by the government — is cause for concern.
Pakistan’s children face enough challenges; the state must do all it can to protect them from online harm.
But combining steps against cyberbullying and online abuse of children with the state’s campaign against ‘fake news’ needs to be reconsidered.

stories.title: Pakistan embassy rejects reports of attack on ambassador in Tehran as ‘baseless’
summary: The Embassy of Pakistan in Tehran categorically rejected reports circulating on social media and other forums concerning Ambassador Imran Ahmed Siddiqui, describing them as baseless and factually incorrect.

The Embassy of Pakistan in Tehran has taken note of certain reports circulating in social media and other forums concerning Ambassador Imran Ahmed Siddiqui, Ambassador of Pakistan to the Islamic Republic of Iran.

The Embassy categorically clarifies that these reports are… — Embassy of Pakistan, Iran (@PakinIran) November 1, 2026 Earlier, reports had emerged that Siddiqui was attacked in the Iranian capital, Tehran.

stories.title: Till I am here, people of KP will have the first right to its resources: Kundi
summary: The governor, who has assumed the administrative control of KP following the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in the province, assured that his priority was the protection of the people of KP, then of the province itself and then Pakistan.
He had also questioned the government’s position on mineral resources during a National Assembly session earlier this week, when he had criticised the Centre over emergency and governor’s rule in KP.
Less than a week after emergency and governor’s rule were imposed in the province, a joint sitting of parliament approved the federal government’s move amid a strong protest from the opposition.

stories.title: Thousands protest in India's capital against voter roll revision
summary: Thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India’s capital on Sunday, renewing demands for the country’s election chief to resign over an overhaul of voter lists they say unfairly benefits the ruling party.

The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The cost of living is going up… The only option is to take to the streets peacefully.” The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online youth-led protest movement, has also thrown its weight behind the campaign against the voter-roll revision.

stories.title: Pakistan's polio tally reaches eight with new case in K-P
summary: The National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication confirmed Pakistan’s seventh polio case of the year, reported from Khyber district of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).

Read: Karachi polio case takes Pakistan’s tally to seven this year Of the seven cases reported across the country so far this year, six have emerged from K-P and one from Sindh, according to the NEOC.

Also Read: First wild polio case of 2026 confirmed in Sindh According to the NEOC, Pakistan has conducted four large-scale polio vaccination campaigns this year, targeting more than 45 million children.

stories.title: China unveils detailed plan for manned moon landing
summary: China will adopt a "two launches, lunar orbit rendezvous" architecture for its manned lunar exploration program, a senior engineer said on Saturday, as development work for lunar landing advances steadily.

Wang said the approach matches China's existing technical capabilities and infrastructure, and the separate development of the spaceship and lunar lander can help standardize production and support the formation of a long-term family of vehicles.
So far, the development of the Long March-10 carrier rocket, the Mengzhou crewed spaceship and the Lanyue lunar lander has been progressing smoothly.

stories.title: Researchers discover first fully marine stem amphibian in Late Triassic fossils
summary: A group of international researchers has reported the first fully marine species of stem amphibian, Gerrothorax maritimus, in a recent research article published in the journal Nature Ecology & Evolution.
More than 8,000 amphibian species exist today, but none of them lives entirely in the sea.
The researchers suggested that Gerrothorax maritimus's flattened body suited life on the seafloor, allowing it to hide in sediments.

stories.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missile, drone targeting kingdom
summary: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a statement that the operation took place on Sunday morning following continued Houthi attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

The Houthis had reported at least 14 deaths in Saudi strikes on a petrol station and market on Wednesday, while the group also targeted the airport in Aden, a stronghold of Yemen's internationally recognised government, wounding civilians.

stories.title: Pillion riding, display of weapons banned in KP's Bannu for a week as polio vaccination drive set to begin
summary: BANNU: The district administration banned pillion riding, display of weapons and use of tinted glasses in vehicles for a week in Bannu on Sunday, keeping in view the commencement of a polio vaccination drive and security concerns.

The order, seen by Dawn, stated that Bannu’s district police officer (DPO) had informed the administration through an official letter that an anti-polio campaign would be conducted in the district from November 2 to 5.
Polio vaccination drive launched DC Khattak and DPO Shafiullah Gandapur inaugurated the anti-polio campaign in Bannu on Sunday, administering polio drops to children.

stories.title: Alibaba partners with Apple to integrate Qwen AI model into Apple Intelligence for Chinese market
summary: Chinese tech company Alibaba Group has partnered with Apple to integrate its Qwen AI model into Apple Intelligence for the Chinese market, state-run Xinhua news agency reported Saturday.
4 and will launch with the official iOS 27.3 release in December, Alibaba said.
Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the partnership would bring new AI-powered services to Chinese users.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza - medics say
summary: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on ​Sunday, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry.
Israeli strikes killed eight people, including a child, in Gaza on Sunday, according to emergency services and local hospitals.
At least 1,500 Palestinians ​have ⁠been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed.

stories.title: Broken record: constitution, commander, curfew.
summary: The issues of Dawn from Sept 1-7, 1947 chronicled the adoption of the Pakistan (Provisional Constitution) Order as the country’s working constitution, while the nation’s first commander-in-chief issued a stern call for order to control communal violence.
Moreover, the city of Karachi — which has been no stranger to violence over the decades — saw its first curfew as the capital of Pakistan.

The lede story in the Sept 3, 1947, edition noted that “the Pakistan (Provisional Constitution) Order, an adaptation of the Government of India Act, 1935” would serve as the dominion’s temporary constitution.

stories.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as drones damage Russian facility
summary: Russian strikes left hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, while Russian authorities reported major damage to an industrial site following Ukrainian drone attacks on Nizhny Novgorod region.
He said Ukraine, meanwhile, had hit the Kamensky plant in Russia's Rostov region, which he said was involved in the manufacture of Russian missiles.

Read: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal could be near ahead of December’s G20 summit In Nizhny Novgorod region, however, Governor Gleb Nikitin said a large-scale overnight Ukrainian drone attack caused "significant damage" to an industrial facility.

stories.title: Xiaomi's October EV deliveries top 50,000, hit 2026 monthly high
summary: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi ​said on Sunday it ‌delivered more than 50,000 electric vehicles ​in October, the ​highest monthly total this ⁠year, as it ​ramps up production ​to meet its 2026 target.
Deliveries reached about 336,000 vehicles ​for the ​first 10 months after topping ‌30,000 ⁠units in August and 40,000 in September.

stories.title: Five killed in fresh ethnic violence in India's Manipur state
summary: Five people were killed in two separate incidents in India's northeastern state of Manipur, police said on Sunday, as fresh ethnic violence erupted in the conflict-hit region.

Read: Manipur: the crisis India doesn't fully confront The predominantly Christian Kuki and Naga tribes have a long history of conflict over competing claims to ethnic homelands in the remote northeastern state.

The latest Kuki-Naga clashes have added to tensions in Manipur, where the Kuki community is also embroiled in a bloody ethnic conflict with the mainly Hindu Meitei community that began in May 2023 over economic benefits and job quotas.

stories.title: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads: KCNA
summary: North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads, its state media reported on Sunday, the latest in a slew of weapons drills aimed at training its military units on using them.

Saturday’s test was conducted to “assess adaptation to combat and power of a cluster-bomb warhead to be tipped on tactical ballistic missiles”, the official Korean Central News Agency reported on Sunday.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was not present on Saturday, although he had overseen a test-launch of cluster-bomb warheads mounted on a ballistic missile in April, accompanied by his daughter Ju Ae.

stories.title: Binance to resume withdrawals after covering bulk of stolen $6.3bn
summary: Binance, the worlds biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals on Sunday after covering 95 per cent of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world’s largest digital heist, which the FBI has tied to North Korea.
Binance said on Sunday it had covered $6bn of stolen cryptocurrencies by using company money to buy replacement tokens.
Analysts had blamed North Korea and said the Binance theft could be the largest financial heist of all time.

stories.title: PIA welcomes its first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner in Islamabad
summary: Pakistan International Airlines’ (PIA) first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner arrived in Islamabad from London on Sunday, marking a new development in the national carrier’s efforts to modernise its fleet and expand international operations.

Reacting to its arrival, Aircraft Owners and Operators Association (AOOA) Pakistan said the induction of the Dreamliner was an important milestone for PIA and a significant step towards the airline’s revival.

Read: Norse Atlantic lands lease deal with PIA It said punctual flights and quality facilities should be among PIA’s priorities, adding that the airline needed to regain passengers’ confidence through a modern booking system and better customer service.

stories.title: Tim Seifert powers New Zealand victory
summary: The result wasn't enough for New Zealand to salvage the series, which the tourists won 3-2 after winning the first three games.

Seifert scored just 36 runs across the first four matches but the big-hitting right-hander found his touch at Seddon Park, swinging the game in New Zealand's favour by blasting 11 fours and five sixes.
Phillips's 341 runs across the five games was the most scored by any batsman in a bilateral T20 series.

stories.title: Israeli Democrats leader warns Netanyahu could use new attack on Iran to stay in power
summary: Israeli Democrats leader Yair Golan warned Sunday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could exploit a potential new military attack on Iran to remain in power amid political uncertainty following last week's elections.
Golan said Netanyahu "lacks the moral legitimacy, and even the basic capacity" to manage another conflict with Iran.
Preliminary results showed Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Jewish opposition parties and 19 for Palestinian parties.

stories.title: Official records ‘stolen’ from Bannu TMA office
summary: BANNU: The theft of official records from the Tehsil Municipal Administration (TMA), Bannu, has come to light, with important registers and files reportedly missing from the Tehsil Officer Regulation (TOR) branch.
In a complaint submitted to the city police station, the administration said that the drawers and cupboards of the branch were found unlocked when the office reopened last Monday.
TMA Bannu Tehsil Municipal Officer Fakhrul Islam requested the police to register a first information report and launch an investigation to recover the missing official records.

stories.title: 12 dilapidated classrooms of Charsadda school sealed
summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Secretary Dr Mohammad Fakhre Alam Irfan had taken notice of the dilapidated condition of the school building after reports and photographs highlighting the plight of students went viral on social media.
DEO Fazal Wahid visited the school accompanied by deputy DEO Zubair Khalil, DEO planning and development Shiraz Hussain and other officials.
The school principal, Mohammad Ayaz Khan, briefed the officials on the deteriorating condition of the building, difficulties faced by students and the impact on academic activities.

stories.title: Woman dies by suicide after ‘strangling’ minor daughter in Bajaur
summary: BAJAUR: A woman allegedly committed suicide after ‘strangling’ her minor daughter to death in War Mamond tehsil of Bajaur district on Saturday, police and residents said.
A police official told Dawn that a team rushed to the spot after receiving information about the incident and the bodies were taken to the District Headquarters Hospital in Khar for postmortem.
Mansoor Khan, a spokesperson for the district police, told reporters that an investigation had been launched to ascertain the causes behind the incident.
